ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a large semicircle, whose horizontal base is labeled as diameter 2; on top of the large semicircle there is a smaller semicircle, whose dashed horizontal diameter is labeled 1. The gray shaded region is inside the small semicircle, but above the arc of the large semicircle, that is, the small semicircle with the part overlapping the large semicircle removed. Reasoning: According to the problem statement and the image, regard the large semicircle as a semicircle with radius 1 and center at the midpoint of its diameter. The diameter of the small semicircle is a horizontal chord on the large circle, with length 1, so the chord endpoints may be taken as x = ±1/2. The equation of the large circle is x^2 + y^2 = 1, therefore the height of the chord is y = sqrt(1 - (1/2)^2) = sqrt(3)/2. The radius of the small semicircle is 1/2, and its area is (1/2)π(1/2)^2 = π/8. The part of the small semicircle occupied by the large semicircle is the circular segment cut off by the chord of length 1 in the large circle. In a circle with radius 1, chord length 1 corresponds to a central angle satisfying 2 sin(θ/2)=1, so θ=π/3. The area of this circular segment = sector area - equilateral triangle area = (1/2)(1)^2(π/3) - sqrt(3)/4 = π/6 - sqrt(3)/4. Therefore the lune area = π/8 - (π/6 - sqrt(3)/4) = sqrt(3)/4 - π/24.

method.method_draft: Use circular-segment subtraction. From the image, identify the shaded lune as the part of the upper semicircle of diameter 1 lying above the arc of the larger semicircle of diameter 2. Place the larger semicircle with radius 1 and center at the midpoint of its diameter. The endpoints of the smaller diameter form a horizontal chord of the large circle of length 1, so if the chord endpoints are at x = ±1/2, their height on the large circle is sqrt(1 - (1/2)^2) = sqrt(3)/2. The area of the smaller semicircle is (1/2)π(1/2)^2 = π/8. The part of the larger semicircle intruding into it is the circular segment cut off by a chord of length 1 in a circle of radius 1. This chord subtends central angle π/3, so the segment area is sector area π/6 minus triangle area sqrt(3)/4. Subtract this segment from π/8 to get the lune area: π/8 - (π/6 - sqrt(3)/4) = sqrt(3)/4 - π/24.

推理：按坐标积分法设大半圆直径为 2，因此半径为 1，取其圆心为原点，大半圆方程为 x^2+y^2=1, y\ge 0，顶边曲线为 y=\sqrt{1-x^2}。小半圆的直径是大圆上的一条水平弦，长度为 1，且关于 y 轴对称，所以端点横坐标为 x=\pm \frac12。代入大圆方程得端点纵坐标 y=\sqrt{1-\frac14}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}。因此小半圆所在圆的圆心为 \left(0,\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)，半径为 \frac12，其上半圆曲线为 y=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}+\sqrt{\frac14-x^2}。阴影面积是在 -\frac12\le x\le \frac12 上，小半圆上弧与大半圆上弧的竖直差，所以面积为
\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}+\sqrt{\frac14-x^2}-\sqrt{1-x^2}\right)dx。
